newsitem.title: POLAND: WARSAW BOURSE FLAT, SEEN EXTENDING SIDEWAYS DRIFT.
newsitem.headline: WARSAW BOURSE FLAT, SEEN EXTENDING SIDEWAYS DRIFT.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse was flat in higher turnover on Tuesday but analysts saw little chance for the market to get out of its eight-week horizontal trend amid no fresh fundamental signals.
"There is no power which could push the market in either direction," said Tomasz Cwintal, an analyst at BGZ brokerage.

Analysts said the bourse could swing in its horizontal trend until elections, due in September, although some said drops were likely ahead of big privatisations such as Poland's largest commercial bank, Bank Handlowy, and copper giant KGHM.
But they said any falls were likely to stop before 15,600, the lowest level in the horizontal trend, as any significant slide was likely to spur bargain-hunting buying.
Analysts said construction sector, chemical firms and brewers, such as Zywiec , could outperform the market as they were likely to show good earnings over the next few months.
The main market's WIG index was flat at 16,245.2 points and turnover rose eight percent to 164.8 million zlotys on all three markets as 47 issues rose, 29 fell and 22 were flat.
But analysts said many investors were limiting buying ahead of the polls and were likely to focus on the attractive primary market such as Handlowy's late May offer and KGHM's likely June sale.

NFI units extended Monday's gains on hopes that the ministry would scrap the idea of imposing a tax on capital gains made by the NFIs on the sale of firms in their portfolios and good first quarter results of the funds.
NFI units rose one percent to 153 zlotys at the regular session and to 154.5 zlotys in the continuous trade.
